---
title: "check-removed-content.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that fails a pull request that removes prose which
reappears nowhere in the pull request.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-11-09, review of
[lds#2032](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/lds/pull/2032)) is that content is moved, never deleted.

Removed lines are normalized (markup, links' targets, math, punctuation and case dropped)
and cut into sentences, so a reflow or a change of line breaks is not a removal.
A removed sentence passes when at least `min-overlap` of its word trigrams
occur among the trigrams of the lines the pull request adds, in any checked file.
A moved sentence passes, and so does a lightly reworded one.
Headings, code, YAML, includes, tables, display math, and sentences with fewer than `min-words`
alphabetic words are not examined.

Two opt-outs cover a deliberate removal:

- `removed-content-ok: reason` in the pull request body, or in an added line such as an HTML comment, exempts the whole pull request.
- A deleted file whose path or file name the pull request body names is exempt.

With no base ref the check skips.
The pull request body is read from the event, so the reusable workflow's example stub also runs on `edited`.

## Usage

Copy
[`examples/check-removed-content.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-removed-content.yml)
to `.github/workflows/` in your repository.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `base-ref` | (empty) | Git ref or SHA to diff against; empty skips the check |
| `globs` | `*.qmd *.md` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check |
| `pr-body` | (empty) | Pull request body, searched for the opt-out and for deleted files' names |
| `min-overlap` | `0.6` | Trigram overlap that counts as moved |
| `min-words` | `5` | Fewest alphabetic words of an examined sentence |
| `fail` | `true` | Fail on a finding; `false` gives warnings only |
| `python-version` | `3.x` | Python version to set up |
